confirmed_defects.title: An unresolved claim is tied to one version of the claimant, so any later version of that row orphans it
source: accounting_agent/source_control.py resolve_pending_supersessions line 117: the claimant is looked up by 'h.snapshot_id = claim.snapshot_id'. Once the claimant has a newer version, the recorded claim matches nothing and is never linked.

accounting_agent/service.py context lines 260-262: the unresolved flag is shown only when the claim's own snapshot is in the period population, so SOURCE_TRANSITION_UNRESOLVED disappears from the newer version even before the target arrives.

accounting_agent/source_control.py supersession_link lines 59-60: a recorded link, by contrast, belongs to the source identity (latest link of the key), so a link survives a revision of the claimant. A pending claim does not.

A newer version without the claim arises in two ordinary ways: the row is revised (amount, description) and the provider does not repeat the claim; or the row was retired by its own replacement and is then re-sent unchanged, which line 30 turns into a new version because the removed flag differs.

smallest_sufficient_correction: Treat a pending claim as belonging to the source identity (kind and key), as links already do: the governing pending claim of an identity is its most recent SOURCE_SUPERSESSION_UNRESOLVED event, for as long as the identity has no link.

In resolve_pending_supersessions, for each identity with such a claim, link the target's head to the claimant's current head (removed or not), keeping the existing cycle refusal and approved-source events.
In context (service.py lines 260-262), report the claim as unresolved for whichever version of the identity is in the population.
No schema change is needed: both the events and the links already exist.

structural_note: This is the third review in a row in which the reproductions in the ticket pass and a neighbouring delivery order fails. The orders are not unrelated: every one is a case where a replacement claim exists in a different form (a link row, an event tied to a snapshot, or only the stored packet) from the one the quarantine decision reads. The 120-order search in fable_rc_order_search.py tests the requirement itself and should be kept in the gate, so that the next pass is measured against the invariant and not against a list of orders. It covers a three-link chain, one unclaimed delivery, one revision and one withdrawal; it is evidence for those deliveries, not proof for every possible feed.

decisions_requiring_client_authority: Feed semantics (gate G2): whether a provider can void a row in a closed cycle, deliver a replacement before the row it replaces, declare a link in a later message, or omit an earlier claim from a later version of a row; whether a removed replacement restores the original; and whether replacing an already withdrawn charge needs the closed period reopened (UC-14). If the provider contract guarantees that a replaced row always arrives before its replacement and that claims arrive with the row, RC-03, RD-01 and RD-02 cannot occur; without that guarantee they can.

The decisions listed in FABLE_RB_CORRECTIONS.json (document policy, statement policy, separation of policy approval and review, treatment of fees and payments, close checklist, authority to disposition, finalize and lock) are unchanged and remain open.
